corrected_value.title: Coordination in the Presence of Asset Markets

decisions.quote: Experimental Economics Replication Project Replication of Coordination in the Presence of Asset Markets by Kogan, S./Kwasnica, A.M./Weber, R.A. (2011) in: The American Economic Review, 101(2), pp. 927–947. Replication Authors: Felix Holzmeister, Jürgen Huber, Michael Kirchler and Michael Razen Kogan et al. test whether there are market communication effects in a “second-order statistic” coordination game, where portfolio incentive effects are absent, when there is a preplay asset market compared to when there is no such market. They find that a preplay market significantly diminishes output in the coordination game compared to the control treatment without a preceding asset market. Hypothesis to bet on: The presence of a preplay asset market lowers output in a “second-order statistic” coordination game (a comparison of group output of the insider groups in the market treatment and the control treatment in Experiment 2).
decisions.location: Primary Project Replication Report for Kogan et al. (2011), p. 1/4 (line 1342)
decisions.reason: Both shipped row 2096 and blind target 16 identify the same replicated original study: Kogan, Kwasnica, and Weber (2011), 'Coordination in the Presence of Asset Markets', Am. Econ. Rev. 101(2), 927–947 (Reference 49). Whereas the earlier blind coding spliced non-contiguous lines from Section 1 and Table S1, this literal contiguous passage from Kogan et al.'s individual primary replication report directly identifies the tested original paper and hypothesis (Experiment 2).

decisions.quote: Given the criteria and procedure outlined above, the hypothesis of interest has been replicated at a significance level of α < 5%. The relative effect size equals 92.52% and the p-value of the hypothesis test is 0.001. References Palan, S. (2015): “GIMS-Software for asset market experiments”, Journal of Behavioral and Experimental Finance, Vol. 5, pp. 1–14. decisions.reason: In the individual primary replication report for Kogan et al. (2011), the authors explicitly conclude that the hypothesis of interest was replicated at alpha < 5% (ordered probit coefficient = -2.534, p = 0.001, relative effect size = 92.52%), matching Table S1 ('Replicated: Yes'). Including the target-specific sentences and Table 1 from Kogan et al.'s individual report resolves the ambiguity of quoting the generic boilerplate sentence alone. Both shipped and blind correctly code the outcome as 'successful'.

decisions.quote: Differences from Original Study The replication procedure is identical to that of the original study, with some unavoidable deviations. This replication will be performed at the University of Innsbruck, Austria, in 2015, on students from the University of Innsbruck, while the original data was gathered at the Laboratory for Economic Management and Auctions at Pennsylvania State University in University Park, USA, in 2006–2007, with subjects from the same lab. The experiment will be conducted in German and not in English as in the original study. The paper studies a number of treatments differentiating between insiders and outsiders as well as different incentives of the market relative to the coordination game (market L vs. market H) in two different experiments. For replication, the focus is only on the comparison between insider groups and the control group in Experiment 2. (The second experiment in the original study only includes the market L treatment as well.)
decisions.location: Primary Project Replication Report for Kogan et al. (2011), Differences from Original Study, p. 2/4 (line 1342)
decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind correctly code the record type as 'replication'. The individual primary replication report for Kogan et al. (2011) confirms that new experimental data were collected in 2015 on a fresh sample of 90 students at the University of Innsbruck to re-test the finding of Experiment 2 from Kogan et al. (2011).
